overview: Confidential Santiago despatch: unverified rumor that three convoyed Japanese ships would reach Valparaíso found no customs or dock-reservation confirmation, though a consul's source quoted Kanamori claiming the convoy aimed to demonstrate against U.S. Pacific power.

people.name: Claude G. Bowers
people.role: Sender of the U.S. Embassy despatch

people.name: Kanamori
people.role: Japanese representative of Itoh y Cia.; identification described as approximate

subfiles.title: Despatch on rumored arrival of convoyed Japanese merchant vessels at Valparaíso
subfiles.from: Claude G. Bowers, U.S. Embassy, Santiago
subfiles.to: The Secretary of State, Washington, D.C.
subfiles.about: Reports and evaluates an unconfirmed rumor that three Japanese merchant ships under heavy naval escort would soon arrive at Valparaíso.
subfiles.summary: Embassy found no confirmed dock reservation or register entry for three rumored Japanese vessels at Valparaíso; the naval attaché couldn't confirm it either, but a consul's memo cited Kanamori's claim of an armed convoy meant to undermine confidence in U.S. Pacific control.

interest: Shows U.S. skepticism and spy-sourced claims about a rumored Japanese convoy nearing Valparaíso in wartime.
